conventions.leaf: {prim, params, transform: {rotate: [{axis: x|y|z|[x,y,z], deg}], translate: [x,y,z]}}; rotations apply in list order, then the translation
conventions.node: {op: union|subtract|intersect, children: [a, b]}; subtract is children[0] minus children[1]
conventions.cylinder: params {radius, height}; axis +Z from z=0 to z=height
conventions.cone: params {r1 (at z=0), r2 (at z=height), height}; r1 or r2 may be 0 (apex)
conventions.torus: params {major, minor}; axis +Z, centred on the origin
conventions.prism: params {points: [[x,y],...] simple polygon, height}; extruded +Z from z=0
conventions.brep: params {source: gzipped wonky-acceptance-operands/1 JSON, body: index}; the exact B-rep body as stored (identity transform); tessellated by scripts/bakeoff/brep-tessellate.mjs
conventions.deviationMm: stated bound on the distance between a leaf tessellation and its analytic surface
conventions.expect: solid (a valid closed 2-manifold mesh, possibly several components) | empty (valid answer is an ok mesh with 0 triangles) | non-manifold-contact (the exact result touches itself along a line or point; a closed 2-manifold mesh of it does not exist, so the expected answer is unresolved with a reason; a mesh is reported but not scored as a pass)

cases.fdmRationale: A single primitive with no Boolean (a plain printed spacer): the result is the operand itself.
Two blocks glued into one print; generic position, no coincident faces.
Notch cut into a block (a slot for a mating part).
Trimming a part to a bounding block (build-volume clip).
Oblique trim of a block; no axis alignment, every intersection edge is skew.
Lip added flush with the top surface; the two top faces are coplanar and overlap.
Rebate cut flush with the top and three sides; cutter faces coincide with stock faces.
Two modelled halves that share one full face; the union must merge into one block with no internal wall.
A tab welded to a wall; the contact face is a sub-rectangle of the wall face.
M6 clearance hole through a 5 mm plate.
Blind hole 3 mm deep for a heat-set insert: a cylinder cut ending in a flat floor inside the plate.
Rectangular pocket 3 mm deep for a magnet or PCB.
M3 socket-head counterbore: coaxial hole and bore, the bore floor is an annulus.
M4 countersink (90 deg cone) meeting a coaxial hole; the cone bottom circle coincides with the hole wall.
Mounting plate with four corner holes.
Perforated panel / speaker grille: 100 holes, many independent intersection loops.
Four holes drilled at 17 deg (angled cable pass-throughs); elliptical entry and exit loops.
Printed pipe tee: perpendicular cylinder union, then the bores; saddle-shaped intersection curves.
Equal-radius crossing cylinders: the intersection curves cross at singular points.
Cross-shaped pipe junction with equal radii (same singular intersection as the intersect case).
Two coaxial equal-radius cylinders overlapping in height (stacked extrusions): coincident curved faces and coplanar facets.
Dome: a sphere cut flat so it sits on the bed.
Ball knob trimmed to a cylindrical envelope.
Ball-joint socket: spherical cavity opening through the top face.
M8 hex nut: hex prism minus bore, intersected with a 30 deg chamfer cone whose top cap is coplanar with the nut top.
Open-top electronics enclosure: shell, four screw bosses with pilot holes, a USB cut-out and a round vent.
Spur-gear blank: 48-tooth concave prism (240 side faces) minus a bore.
Round rod resting on a block: the cylinder touches the top face along one line (tessellation vertices lie exactly on it).
Hole placed so its wall just touches the plate side face (a common layout slip); tangent along a line.
A union with an identical copy (duplicated body in a slicer project): A u A = A.
Subtracting an identical copy: A - A is empty (expected result volume 0).
Intersecting an identical copy: A n A = A.
Sealed internal cavity (weight reduction / embedded magnet pocket): one solid bounded by two shells.
Two separate parts on one plate: union of disjoint bodies, two components.
Pin header / peg board: a left-deep chain of 20 unions, each pin sunk 1 mm into the base.
Two finely tessellated overlapping spheres (~50k input triangles): throughput case.
O-ring / handle cut in half so it prints flat; the cut plane passes through a ring of tessellation vertices.

The frozen r10b UpperCore g10 UNION operands (exact B-rep, 82 planar faces vs 40 planar + 10 cylindrical faces incl. an ellipse edge) on which the exact general-fuse route stalled; a real printed part.
